records.title: Strait of Hormuz shipping 65% below pre-war levels in mid-November, UKMTO says
records.claim: Iran International published an in-window report on 21 Nov at 03:11 UTC citing UKMTO's 20 Nov weekly statistics: Hormuz vessel transits for the week to 18 Nov fell to 263 from 308 in the preceding week; these are vessel passages, not oil barrel volumes.
records.boundary: In-window article published 21 Nov; underlying UKMTO report is 20 Nov and covers data only through 18 Nov. Do not misstate the week-on-week fall as a new 21 Nov traffic event or translate vessels into oil barrels.
records.support_excerpt: Iran International, 21 Nov 2026 03:11 GMT: UKMTO recorded 263 vessel transits during the week to 18 Nov, down from 308 the previous week; 115 outbound and 148 inbound versus 139 and 169. Original UKMTO overview is dated 20 Nov; vessel counts do not establish oil barrels.

source_identity_receipt.observed_title: Strait of Hormuz shipping 65% below pre-war levels in mid-November, UKMTO says

records.title: The U.A.E. Is Shuttling Oil Past Iran in Risky Hormuz Operation
records.claim: WSJ reports ADNOC organizes risky shuttle tanker operations to support some oil movements through Hormuz, not proof that overall shipping normalizes.
records.boundary: Partial shuttle continuity does not imply normal operations or lower costs
records.support_excerpt: WSJ dated article reports ADNOC expanded its tanker fleet and high-risk shuttle operations to maintain oil movement through Hormuz, under military protection, with material vessel and crew risks.
